concerns.text: The collapse intensity target defined in FR-021 is a deterministic function of the same acoustic parameters (SNR, RT60) that are later used as predictors in the regression model (FR-005). Because the algorithm uses hard‑coded thresholds on SSS and WER derived from those parameters, the regression is guaranteed to learn the rule rather than an independent, universal interaction effect, creating a circular validation.

FR‑021 employs fixed thresholds (SSS < 0.5 and WER > 2× baseline) without any empirical justification, prior literature support, or sensitivity analysis. These arbitrary cut‑offs can bias the identified collapse points and undermine the construct validity of the outcome variable.

While FR‑020 defines a deterministic interpolation rule, the specification provides no plan for a systematic sensitivity analysis of the threshold values or interpolation parameters, violating the requirement to assess how the collapse definition influences downstream regression results.

FR‑001 claims that a sample of ≥ 50 000 clips provides 80 % power to detect an effect size f² ≥ 0.02, yet the power analysis is marked as '[deferred]' and no concrete calculation is presented. Without a verified sample‑size justification, the study may be under‑powered, threatening the scientific validity of any reported effects.
